skill.author: inference-sh-7

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms critical curl pipe-to-shell installer risks. It also confirms high-risk manual installation from a remote manifest. Many API key and documentation-link findings are false positives, but broad infsh permissions and social media actions remain risky.

remediation.issue: Remote installer commands pipe downloaded content into sh.
remediation.suggestion: Remove curl pipe-to-shell examples or replace them with pinned release downloads, checksum verification, signature verification, and explicit user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Manual install derives the binary URL through shell command substitution against a remote manifest.
remediation.suggestion: Publish fixed versioned download URLs and checksums, and avoid parsing remote manifests inside shell commands.

remediation.issue: The allowed Bash pattern permits all infsh subcommands.
remediation.suggestion: Narrow allowed commands where possible and require confirmation before deploy, pull, account, billing, or social media operations.

remediation.issue: The skill documents API key use through INFSH_API_KEY.
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples as placeholders and instruct users not to paste real API keys into prompts, logs, or shared files.

content.user_title: Run Cloud AI Apps with inference.sh
content.value_statement: Teams need one command path for many cloud AI models. This skill guides agents through inference.sh CLI discovery, execution, and task tracking.
actual_capabilities: Explains inference.sh CLI installation, login, update, and API key setup.
Shows how to list, search, filter, and inspect available inference.sh apps.
Guides cloud app runs with inline input, saved input files, and version pinning.
Documents task status checks, saved results, and long-running no-wait jobs.
Includes examples for image, video, LLM, search, audio, 3D, and X/Twitter apps.
Lists related specialized skills for focused AI workflows.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh account and an installed infsh CLI.
Cloud app runs may send prompts, files, or metadata to external services.
Model names, app schemas, prices, and availability can change outside the skill.
Social media actions require account authorization and explicit user review.

use_cases.title: Prototype Multimodal AI Features
use_cases.description: Find image, video, audio, and LLM apps, then run quick tests from one CLI workflow.

use_cases.title: Produce Campaign Assets
use_cases.description: Generate draft images, videos, captions, and search-backed context without switching between many provider tools.

use_cases.title: Operate Long Cloud Jobs
use_cases.description: Submit long-running jobs, track task IDs, and save generated outputs for review or automation.

prompt_templates.title: Find an App
prompt_templates.prompt: List inference.sh apps for image generation, explain the strongest options, and ask before running any command.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Simple Job
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me run a video generation app with my prompt, show the planned command, and wait for my approval first.

prompt_templates.title: Track a Long Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe workflow to generate a sample input, submit a no-wait job, track the task, and save the result.

prompt_templates.title: Review Account Impact
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned infsh workflow, identify data that leaves my machine, and require confirmation before any X/Twitter action.

output_examples.input: Find a model for a product concept image.
output: Suggested image apps are grouped by speed, quality, and provider.
The response explains which app fits product concept work.
The agent asks before running any generation command.

output_examples.input: Run a long video job and monitor it.
output: The workflow prepares a sample input file and submits the job without waiting.
The task ID is tracked until the output is ready.
The final result is saved for local review.
The response separates draft text from account-changing actions.
It requests explicit approval before posting, following, liking, or sending messages.
It notes which account permissions are required.

best_practices: Confirm every command that spends credits, uploads files, posts content, or changes account state.
Use sample inputs and app details before running unfamiliar apps.
Keep API keys in local secret storage and avoid placing real keys in prompts.
anti_patterns: Do not run pipe-to-shell installers without independent review and verification.
Do not submit private files or secrets to cloud apps unless the data flow is approved.
Do not allow automated social posting without a human review step.

faq.question: What does this skill help an agent do?
faq.answer: It helps an agent use the inference.sh CLI to find apps, run cloud AI jobs, and track results.

faq.question: Does it require an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI needs login or an API key before authenticated app runs can work.

faq.question: Can it generate images and videos?
faq.answer: Yes. The references include image, video, audio, LLM, search, 3D, and utility app examples.

faq.question: Can it post to X or Twitter?
faq.answer: The skill includes X/Twitter automation examples. Users should require explicit approval before any account-changing action.

faq.question: Are outputs stored locally?
faq.answer: Some commands can save task results locally, while generated media may be returned as hosted download URLs.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: The install documentation includes remote shell installer patterns and broad CLI permissions that need careful review.
